evidence.quote: Inflation remains below the Federal Reserve's 2 percent symmetric objective, which has been true for most of the past seven years.
More broadly, the balance of risks remains to the downside, although there has been some improvement in risk sentiment in recent weeks.

Given the persistent shortfall of inflation from its target over recent years, this would imply supporting inflation a bit above 2 percent for some time to compensate for the period of underperformance.
A better alternative would have been to delay liftoff until we had achieved our targets.
there may be advantages to an approach that caps interest rates on Treasury securities at the short-to-medium range of the maturity spectrum—yield curve caps

parsed.rationale: The speaker sees a solid near-term outlook but leans dovish: she notes downside risks and below-target inflation, and favors makeup inflation above 2 percent, delayed liftoff and yield curve caps. Near-term guidance is data-dependent after the cuts, so the dovishness is moderate rather than explicit easing.
